A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoT Red-Handed with the same authors, central method and datasets. All 22 pages of each version, including appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original monitoring catch rates, attack-policy experiments, fine-tuning results and task-completion rates, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 reports original monitoring and task-completion results, including additional trusted-model evaluations and pairwise monitor-score correlations.

M1.justification: The hybrid scoring formula and weight of 0.55, final monitor prompts, task-pairing procedure and described attack implementations are retained. Appendix A.1 expands the history of prompt development without changing the final prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use BigCodeBench Instruct with the same eleven side tasks and retain OpenCodeReasoning for fine-tuning. Additional trusted models change model configurations; no new dataset, domain or task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: Both versions compare hybrid monitoring against action-only and CoT-plus-answer monitoring. The additional trusted models instantiate this same comparator set; the competing monitoring protocols are retained.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from GPT-4.1-mini to also include Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite and GPT-4.1-nano. v3 adds full-range ROC-AUC evaluation. Section 2.2 also explicitly documents equal monitor-call budgets, although v2's missing run counts prevent establishing whether that control changed an existing implementation. Dataset splits, success filtering and the primary 1% FPR criterion remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds pairwise monitor-score correlation analysis in Appendix A.5 and qualitative prompt comparisons and failure analysis in A.1. It extends the reported FPR analysis, but removes the displayed few-shot and fine-tuning attack results found in v2 Figures 4, 5, 8 and 9, despite retaining their methodological descriptions. This substantially changes the supplementary and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: v3 first specifies two averaged evaluations for each standalone monitor and one evaluation per hybrid component. This is newly reported repetition information, not an established increase over v2. Both versions display error bars without specifying new confidence levels, seed practices or significance tests.

E6.justification: Detection plots are extensively revised, three trusted-model result sets are added, and few-shot/fine-tuning result entries disappear. v3 Figure 8 newly reports AUCs of 0.797 for hybrid, 0.755 for action-only and 0.760 for CoT. New Figure 4 includes hybrid underperformance, such as Haiku monitoring Sonnet: 42.0% hybrid versus 47.6% action-only. These additions and revisions do not establish same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The hybrid equation, weighting search and task-subtlety criterion are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added empirical ROC and correlation analyses introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the claim of up to 27 percentage points of improvement from CoT monitoring and reduces the stated hybrid advantage on subtle deception from over fourfold to approximately twofold. The central contributions concerning complementary monitoring signals and hybrid monitoring remain.

C2.justification: v3 Section 4.2 develops the interpretation that monitor capability and a sufficient capability threshold matter for detection, while qualifying extrapolation to future models. Appendix A.5 newly interprets lower CoT-score correlations as motivation for diverse monitor ensembles. Most deployment limitations and persuasion explanations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds prompt-selection history, temperature 1.0 and monitor-call allocation details, plus provider/license information for the additional monitors. Final prompts, fine-tuning hyperparameters and hardware information remain unchanged. Existing code and transcript links move to the first-page footnote; they are not newly available resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning relative to SHADE-Arena in Section 2.1 and connects its monitor-capability interpretation to Control Tax in Section 4.2, alongside references for new monitor models. Most prior-work comparisons are retained and reorganized.

P1.justification: The document substantially reorganizes its narrative: Method moves ahead of Related Work, experimental setup is integrated into Method, background material is redistributed, and AI-safety implications move into the conclusion. Hybrid-weight selection moves from its dedicated appendix subsection into the main text, and the transcript-link appendix becomes a footnote.

P2.justification: v3 introduces a four-monitor overview and correlation heatmaps, redraws the FPR analysis as an ROC plot, restructures performance plots and expands Table 6. Figures 1 and 2 remain unchanged. Figure 11 introduces problematic task labeling: its near-zero action-only Log I/O rates conflict with the near-100% rate in Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens monitor evaluation, documents call-budget controls and adds useful prompt and correlation analyses. However, it removes few-shot/fine-tuning result evidence, retains an all-model hybrid-superiority claim contradicted by new Figure 4, and introduces conflicting task labels between Figures 3 and 11. These evidence gains and reporting regressions prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
